findings.reason: the census number gates §3, so a script that re-globs `plan-*.v*.json` and misses the committed tree (which `list_plan_reviews` deliberately reads beside staging) or mixes code reviews into the plan population yields a wrong count that §3 is then decided on, and the fix is one sentence naming the owners.
findings.text: §2 says the census covers "every stored plan review and every delivered plan-review sidecar" across every mounted project, but cites no existing reader for either population and no existing classifier, so the plan proposes a fresh walk where all four mechanisms already exist

findings.reason: extending/calling this owner keeps the "committed copy wins, code reviews excluded" contract that a re-implemented glob would silently drop.
findings.text: the census duplicates the stored-review reader `list_plan_reviews(project=None)`, which already enumerates every stored plan review across the committed tree and the staging root of every mounted project and returns each record's `plan_fingerprint` and `review_path`

findings.reason: this reader already performs the census's sidecar half, so the plan should call it rather than re-discover the report-directory layout.
findings.text: the census duplicates the sidecar reader `delivered_reports` (and its code sibling `delivered_code_reviews`, `reckon/crew/plan_review.py:2009`) over `_delivered_report_sidecars` (`reckon/crew/plan_review.py:1925`), which already enumerates delivered sidecars and filters them by exactly `_fingerprint_forms`' three digests

findings.reason: re-deriving the three digests in a census script lets the census's notion of "matches only the pre-collapse form" drift from the production reader whose retirement §3 performs.
findings.text: the census's core classification (which of the three forms a stored review matches against the current snapshot) is already expressed by `_fingerprint_forms` plus the membership test at `reckon/crew/plan_review.py:823-824` (`forms = _fingerprint_forms(content)`; `whole = [record for record in records if record.get("plan_fingerprint") in forms]`), which the plan does not name

findings.reason: this is a runtime safety check whose result does not gate §3's count, so although the owner should be named, getting it wrong does not change the plan's shape.
findings.text: §2's third census item ("any live run whose write paths claim `reckon/crew/plan_review.py` or `reckon/_store.py`") duplicates the crew claim reader `declared_claim_paths` (`reckon/crew/claims.py:85`) and the repository-scope claims reader `_repository_scope_claims` (`reckon/crew/dispatch_claims.py:223`) already surfaced by the crew `scopes` view

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the plan adds no module and hides no behaviour behind a new interface; §3 removes an op and a fingerprint form, which is depth-reducing rather than surface-spreading.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the §2 census re-walks the review store and re-reads live write-path claims instead of calling the modules that already own those reads, so the census duplicates `list_plan_reviews`/`delivered_reports`/`_fingerprint_forms` and the crew claim reader.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1685, cli_options 349, mcp_views 34, refusal_families 23; §3 retires an MCP op (`collapse_section`, `reckon/mcp.py:1269`) and a fingerprint form and adds nothing to any family, so it names its retirement rather than adding surface.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §2 proposes a census script but names none of the review-store machinery it needs: the store reader `list_plan_reviews` (`reckon/crew/plan_review.py:1074`), the delivered-sidecar reader `delivered_reports` (`reckon/crew/plan_review.py:1973`) over `_delivered_report_sidecars` (`reckon/crew/plan_review.py:1925`), the classifier `_fingerprint_forms` (`reckon/crew/plan_review.py:678`), or the live-claim reader `declared_claim_paths` (`reckon/crew/claims.py:85`).
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the plan adds no durable wrapper layer over existing machinery; §2's census is a one-off read delivered as evidence, not a thin shim left in production code.
